newsitem.title: NORWAY: Norway shares move into reverse, investors cautiou.
newsitem.headline: Norway shares move into reverse, investors cautiou.

text.p: Norwegian shares went into reverse on Thursday following the trend other European markets and on investor uncertainty over economic developments at home, brokers said.
The down move was a slight 0.18 percent off the Total share index, which closed at 879.54 points, but signalled a return of cautiousness to the share market, they said.

"It's a bit of profit-taking in some of the shares that have done well recently, but there are people who are beginning to worry about how fast the (Norwegian) economy is running and inflation," said one dealer.
Turnover was a booming 1.4 billion crowns, which included 573 million crowns in trade from the acquisition of outstanding Transocean ASA shares by merged group Transocean Offshore Inc.

Insurer Storebrand dropped 1.10 crowns to 35.70 crowns in continuation of the slide since it posted weaker-than-expected third quarter resuslts. Dealers said the market was disappointed with the non-life sector.
Storebrand accounted for 114 million crowns of business.
Shipbuilding and engineering group Kvaerner relinquished almost two percent to 250.50 crowns, mainly on reports that it had failed to sell off luxury liner Cunard, brokers said.
